_comment: STAGE-D per-batch coverage registry -- batch 'analog_schedule' (D18, Tier-2 frontend cluster)
(docs/SIMULATOR.md SS12.3/12.4; full-coverage program;
work-list docs/SIMULATOR.md D18).
Run via tests/harness/gate.py <this file> (L0+L1; calls tests/harness/coverage_audit.py) and
tests/harness/mutation.py <this file> (L2).
MODULE: frontend/analog_schedule.py -- the Axis-1 substep-schedule IR + the schedule compilers
+ the process-lifetime compiler seal. Five frozen dataclasses (DurationBracket / DurationPolicy /
SubstepOperation / AnalogSubstepIR / SubstepSchedule) whose load-bearing __post_init__ coerces +
validates fields and each expose a to_manifest; DurationPolicy adds bracket_for; three compilers
(compile_code_spec_to_substep_schedule -> circuit_ir_to_substep_schedule -> the CircuitIR
extractor, plus stim_circuit_to_substep_schedule the read-only Stim importer); the preregistered
h3_h5_duration_policy table; and the seal pair has_valid_compiler_schedule_seal /
require_compiler_schedule_seal. The module imports NEITHER torch NOR quimb (dataclasses + hashlib
+ hmac + json + secrets + sibling frontend imports), so EVERY public unit is CPU-PURE and IN-SCOPE
for full L0+L1+L2 -- out_of_scope is therefore {} (the AST reconcile refuses any gpu_bound claim
on a torch-less module).
SEVENTEEN public units (AST reconcile _public_units_in_module: top-level public defs + every
public method of a top-level class + the load-bearing __post_init__ dunder of each frozen
dataclass). Every dataclass here HAS a __post_init__ (all five contribute one). The many
module-level private helpers (_extract_substeps / _make_substep / _make_barrier_substep /
_operation_from_step / _gate_kind / _gate_participants / _explicit_duration_ns / _active_qubits /
_explicit_idle_qubits / _mechanism_slots_for / _reject_projected_or_noisy_circuit /
_find_axis2_source_metadata_path / _stim_circuit_to_circuit_ir / _stim_qubit_target /
_stim_record_keys / _schedule_template_name / _qubit_metadata / _static_zz_* / _record_layout_ref /
_circuit_ir_manifest / _step_manifest / _stable_hash / _jsonable / _sorted_unique / the seal seams
_seal_compiler_schedule / _compiler_schedule_signature / _schedule_signature_manifest) and the
nested flush() are NOT units (not reconciled/scored), but ARE exercised + mutation-covered through
the public compiler/importer paths (mutmut is coverage-guided). The unit set:
* 5 dataclass __post_init__: DurationBracket / DurationPolicy / SubstepOperation /
AnalogSubstepIR / SubstepSchedule.
* 5 dataclass to_manifest: DurationBracket / DurationPolicy / SubstepOperation /
AnalogSubstepIR / SubstepSchedule.
* DurationPolicy.bracket_for.
* h3_h5_duration_policy.
* compile_code_spec_to_substep_schedule / circuit_ir_to_substep_schedule /
stim_circuit_to_substep_schedule.
* has_valid_compiler_schedule_seal / require_compiler_schedule_seal.
CPU discipline. Every unit runs on plain-Python dataclass construction + Stim/CircuitIR frontend
compilation (no torch, no simulator dynamics), so the tests are fast + deterministic.
L2 DISCIPLINE (100% coverage != discrimination). The compilers build a curated small circuit and
the resulting SubstepSchedule is pinned by an INDEPENDENT recompute of the schedule structure --
the ordered substep kinds, per-substep operations/active-idle/duration bracket, mechanism slots,
participants, window support, and record layout -- and each dataclass to_manifest is pinned to its
EXACT dict (coerced to lists). The h3_h5_duration_policy is pinned to its EXACT six-bracket table
reconstructed by hand, NOT read back from the module. Every coercion is made observable by feeding
NON-canonical typed inputs (int index -> str kind, int ns -> float, lowercase name -> upper,
int-1 -> bool True) and pinning the coerced value+type (kills the object.__setattr__(self,
'<field>', ...) attribute-name string mutants).
RAISING-GUARD ROUTE COVERAGE (the D13 guard-route lesson): every validation raise is tripped with
the EXACT message via str(excinfo.value)==... through EVERY input route that reaches it:
* DurationBracket: low<0 (via -1<=low with high>=low so the `or` is killed, not just the branch),
high<low, nominal-outside-bracket, bad epistemic_class.
* DurationPolicy: empty-brackets, duplicate-kind.
* DurationPolicy.bracket_for: unknown-kind (over the multi-bracket h3_h5 table so the loop
no-match arc runs).
* SubstepOperation: negative target (mixed (0,-1) kills any->all).
* AnalogSubstepIR: tick<0 / order<0 (both `or` operands), nominal<=0, dt_bracket[0]<0 /
dt_bracket[1]<dt_bracket[0] (both `or` operands), bad epistemic_class.
* SubstepSchedule: num_qubits<=0, empty source_hash, wrong representability, per-substep
order_index mismatch, window qubit outside [0, num_qubits).
* circuit_ir_to_substep_schedule: the reserved-source_kind guard tripped via the public route
(source_kind!='circuit_ir' WITHOUT the authority sentinel), the _reject noise_projection
guard through BOTH the dict-projection ('type' extracted) AND the non-dict-projection arcs,
and the source-projection-audit guard; the unsupported-gate / odd-two-qubit / self-pair /
overlapping-pair / unsupported-measurement / idle-two-args / idle-nonpositive-duration /
grouped-inconsistent-duration raises (through the private extraction seams).
* stim_circuit_to_substep_schedule: SHIFT_COORDS, embedded-noise, non-qubit-target,
unsupported-instruction (CXSWAP reaches the final raise), and QUBIT_COORDS multi-target.
* require_compiler_schedule_seal: the seal raise tripped through the UNSEALED route (a schedule
built by hand, not via a compiler -> _compiler_signature is None); has_valid also probed on a
genuinely sealed schedule (True) AND a TAMPERED one (a wrong non-empty signature -> the
hmac.compare_digest arc runs and returns False).
BRANCH-into-guard PROBES (the D13 default-arg/default-branch reachability rule):
* circuit_ir_to_substep_schedule's `source_hash or _stable_hash(...)` and `duration_policy or
h3_h5_duration_policy()` are each exercised BOTH ways -- an explicit source_hash + a custom
DurationPolicy are passed and PINNED as used (kills the or->and mutant that would fall back to
the default), and the default (None) arcs run in the base circuit path.
* SubstepSchedule's `{} if context.is_trivial else context.to_manifest()` and to_manifest's
`if self.axis1_local_lindblad_context:` are exercised with a NON-trivial context (a hand-built
schedule carrying axis1_local_lindblad_context) AND a trivial one; the compiler-provenance
seal_present/generated_substeps arcs run sealed (compiler) AND unsealed (hand-built).
* DEAD-DEFENSIVE, probed not assumed: the _find_axis2_source_metadata_path arm of
_reject_projected_or_noisy_circuit is UNREACHABLE for a validly-constructed CircuitIR because
CircuitIR.__post_init__'s validate_public_metadata already rejects every axis-2 source key
(source_timeline/source_binding/source_payload/source_process/source_fanout are all in
metadata_guard._RESERVED_METADATA_KEY_PARTS). The test PROVES the earlier guard fires (building
a CircuitIR with a 'source_process' key raises at construction), so no route reaches the
schedule extractor with such a circuit. Any surviving mutant on that dead arc is a genuine
equivalent (src-cleanup candidate, not edited here).
NO exemptions + NO out_of_scope: every public unit is CPU-pure and every guard is REACHABLE
through a constructor/compiler route (checked, not assumed).
